rerouted_sites: for each route entry in network['routes'], warehouse = r['from'], site = r['to'], compare best_route vs passable_route, collect site id when routes differ, dedupe, sorted.

But then "no delivery uses a road its vehicle may not use" — a site with no usable route can't be served anyway. If passable returns None, "the chosen routes differ" — a strict reading would include the site. But the ticket says passable_route finds a route that is different — None isn't a route. This is a minor ambiguity. Also, if best_route returns None (no routes at all), both None → same, not counted. Fine.

The plan relies on R1 for semantics. That's fine — the plan says "determine usability with can_pass (R1)". Since P2 is one step of a plan, can_pass being added elsewhere is fine.

Check: does the plan's truck-preference logic match ticket? "sending a truck if a truck may use every road on that route and a van otherwise" — yes, per-route. And "shortest usable route" — min by (km, id) matching best_route ordering. Yes.

One more check: rerouted_sites iterates network['routes'] entries — dedupe via set, sorted. Sites in name order — sorted ids. Ticket says "in name order" — sorted site ids. Fine.

The None edge: should I reject? The verifier instruction: reject only if the item is wrong — a step that would not do what the ticket asks. If passable returns None, the "chosen route" by passable doesn't exist. A reasonable implementer following the plan would compare route objects; None vs dict differ. But also arguably a site where nothing can get through is affected... The ticket's "Done when" focuses on no delivery using blocked roads. Hmm.
